title: Seven stars to watch at Wafcon 2026 and why
description: As the biggest ever Women's Africa Cup of Nations gets ready for kick-off, BBC Sport Africa picks seven players to keep an eye on in Morocco.
fullText:
The 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (Wafcon) kicks off on Sunday, with Nigeria defending their title.

Morocco is hosting for the third time in a row, with the Atlas Lionesses aiming to lift the trophy for the first time after losing back-to-back finals on home soil.

This year's tournament has added importance because qualification for the 2027 Fifa Women's World Cup is on the line, with the four semi-finalists securing a ticket to Brazil.

BBC Sport Africa picks out seven players to watch.

The AFC Toronto forward was the inspiration behind her country's run to a record-extending 10th title last year with two goals and six assists.

Seizing her moment as a starter from the quarter-finals onwards, Okoronkwo combined creativity with some unerring finishing.

With the Super Falcons trailing 2-0 against the hosts in the final, it was the 29-year-old's composed penalty which sparked the comeback.

Okoronkwo then set up Folashade Ijamilusi's equaliser and Jennifier Echegini's late winner to complete a remarkable turnaround.

Despite her impact, Okoronkwo was surprisingly overlooked at the Confederation of African Football awards last year, meaning she may have extra motivation to show what she can do on the big stage.

Malawi are one of two Wafcon debutants and the Lyon forward is the main goal threat for the lowest-ranked nation at the finals, having helped fire her club side to a fifth consecutive league title in France last season.

In 2023, while at Paris St-Germain, she became the first Malawian woman to play and score in the Uefa Champions League.

The 30-year-old is expected to line up in attack alongside younger sister Temwa as the scorchers face a tough group containing Nigeria, Zambia and Egypt.

"I was waiting to qualify for the Africa Cup of Nations [for] a long time," she said.

"I've been playing big games in Europe, but I like to tell the girls 'don't be shy, don't be scared'.

"We can't wait to start and see what we can do."

Is this the final chance for the Atlas Lionesses captain to lift the trophy?

The 35-year-old opened the scoring against Nigeria in last year's final but Morocco were ultimately forced to settle for silver medals again.

Chebbak did pick up the golden boot, netting five times, having been joint top scorer in 2022 when South Africa thwarted Morocco in the final.

And the Al-Hilal forward, who was named African player of the year in November, is also bidding for another unique piece of history.

Her father Larbi helped Morocco to the men's Africa Cup of Nations title in 1976, and Chebbak will hope it is third time lucky for her as she targets a unique double.

The form of the Harambee Starlets goalkeeper will be crucial if the East Africans are to surprise people and make the knockout stage.

Awuor played a vital role in helping Kenya back to the finals for the first time since 2016, saving two penalties in the second leg of their first-round qualifying tie away against Tunisia last February.

The 27-year-old has gained experience since her move to Romanian side Farul Constanta two years ago, helping them secure back-to-back league titles.

Kenya, the second lowest-ranked side at the finals at 128th in the world, take on Morocco, Algeria and Senegal in a tricky Group A.

Ghazi was just 14 the last time Egypt appeared at Wafcon – but was still included in the Cleopatras squad for that tournament in 2016, even if she did not make it on to the pitch.

With a decade of extra experience under her belt, the Al Ahly midfielder, who has battled hard to return to her best after rupturing an anterior cruciate ligament three years ago, is taking inspiration from Egypt's men and their run to the last 16 at the 2026 Fifa World Cup.

"This is the best motivation we could ever get for our women's team," Ghazi said.

"They've filled our hearts with so much joy.

"We have a big responsibility to inspire and keep moving the legacy of Egyptian women's football, especially on the African stage."

Firmly established as one of South Africa's senior leaders, Banyana Banyana's skipper will be looking to help her team reclaim the title they won for the first time in 2022.

"When you look at the number of teams in this year's edition, I think this will be one of the most challenging tournaments we've ever had in the history of Wafcon," said the 33-year-old midfielder, who recently joined an elite group by winning her 150th cap.

At a minimum, South Africa will be looking to reach the last four again, which would guarantee Desiree Ellis' team a place at a third successive World Cup, having reached the last 16 at the 2023 tournament in Australia and New Zealand.

"[The coaching staff] have experienced the team winning the Wafcon and not doing so well. We've got the recipe that you need in order to succeed," Jane added.

South Africa have been drawn alongside Tanzania, Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso in Group B.

The other debutants at this year's finals are Cape Verde, whose women only played their first international in 2018.

Da Luz has been part of the squad since the early days and assumed the captaincy in 2020.

The left-back, who has a degree in systems and computer engineering, leads a side consisting entirely of part-time players.

A serial title winner with Praia-based Seven Stars, Da Luz popped up with two vital goals in qualifying.

She netted in both legs in the first round, a 6-3 aggregate win over Guinea, before the islanders secured their spot on the road in Bamako where they upset Mali, who they will face again after the Eagles also progressed to the finals based on their world ranking.

title: Hamilton leads Ferrari one-two in Hungary practice
description: Lewis Hamilton leads team-mate Charles Leclerc to a Ferrari one-two in Friday practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix.
fullText:
Ferrari led the field by a significant margin in Friday practice at the Hungarian Grand Prix but Charles Leclerc predicted a "tight" qualifying session on Saturday.

Leclerc trailed team-mate Lewis Hamilton by 0.148 seconds with McLaren's Lando Norris 0.499secs back in third place.

Mercedes had a difficult day, championship leader Kimi Antonelli 13th fastest after a disrupted run on soft tyres and George Russell fifth.

The topic of the day was the new Aston Martin, which Fernando Alonso said felt "much better" after an encouraging debut for the team that has been at the back all season.

The veteran two-time champion was 2.990secs off the pace in 19th place but had a lap faster by 0.4secs ruled out for track limits.

Even so, Alonso's actual lap time marked a major step forward for a team that has been trailing by more than four seconds in recent races.

How to follow Hungarian Grand Prix on the BBC

With a new Honda engine due for the next race, the Dutch Grand Prix after Formula 1's summer break, Alonso said there was a "positive atmosphere in the team now".

"The car feels more glued to the ground and easier to drive to an extent when you are in control of the grip in the corners," Alonso added.

"More predictable and an easier car but still a long way to go for us.

"Obviously this will be the first step. We need to find more performance both on the chassis but also on the engine.

"Zandvoort would be a good test for us with the new engine. So step by step but definitely in the right direction."

The key was not only that the upgrade was a step in the right direction but also that it had delivered as expected.

There had been some nervousness around that for the first major upgrade under Adrian Newey's technical leadership. In the past three seasons, upgrades had not delivered as expected, and it was critical for the future that this one, designed and developed with new tools at the team's new factory, worked.

Newey said further upgrades to the car were due for the Italian and Azerbaijan Grands Prix in September.

Alonso said: "We had what we expected in terms of numbers and correlation, which is obviously very encouraging for the future as well, for next year's car and the future upgrades into this year.

"It's still a long way to go for us. Obviously, we're starting so far behind, but this is the first step, hopefully, of good ones coming."

The day was not all positive for Aston Martin, however. Alonso's team-mate Lance Stroll spun out of the first session with what initially appeared to be a rear suspension failure.

He was then unable to take part in the second because there was not enough time to repair the car.

Team representative Pedro de la Rosa said: "It is a suspension failure. We were confident it would not happen in Fernando's car. That's why we sent him out. Because of the lack of spares we couldn't repair his car on time. Some parts need to be repaired and some needed to come here."

Ferrari had been expected to be strong at this track, which is one of the least power-dependent on the calendar, as it has the best car in the corners but it is lacking engine performance.

But Leclerc was cautious about reading too much into it. Hamilton did not speak to the media - only one driver from each team does a pooled interview on Fridays.

"It was a relatively strong day," Leclerc said. "I felt good with the car and the performance seemed to be there straight away so that's a good thing but the weekend is long.

"From the Friday to Saturday we see teams making a jump in performance. Normally we are on the back foot on Friday so it's a good thing we have a good Friday but we still need to stay on it and work hard to get better tomorrow.

"It is going to be tight tomorrow. I don't expect us to have the gap we have today, we will have to do everything perfect. But if the feeling is there I am sure we will do a good job in Q3."

George Russell was 0.933secs off the pace and behind Norris, with a significant upgrade on the McLaren, and Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

The Briton said: "It's a bit of a shame because Budapest is one of the most enjoyable circuits to drive. They have resurfaced a third of the track and they've done a really bad job. It's really bumpy.

"The track is braking up in the last corner so people are driving around the middle of the last corner and not hitting the apex.

"The underlying car pace doesn't seem as competitive as we saw in Silverstone and Spa. There is a lot of room to improve. The wind is shifting a lot and that has a real impact into car balance. Hopefully tomorrow will be better."

Antonelli, leading Hamilton by 45 points and Russell by 50, did not complete a qualifying simulation lap in the second session.

His first had to be abandoned when Franco Colapinto crashed his Alpine at the last corner, and his second came to grief when he made an error going into the chicane.

Antonelli was complaining all session about rear brake locking, but he was on a par with Norris' time in the first sector on both laps before they were curtailed.

Deputy team principal Bradley Lord said: "Lack of grip and balance, both drivers had to wind some front wing out, but on the long runs looked pretty consistent and competitive compared to the Ferrari, Red Bull and McLarens."

Behind Russell, Red Bull's Isack Hadjar was sixth fastest, ahead of Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad completed the top 10.

title: Sinner, Djokovic withdraw from Montreal Masters
description: Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic have pulled out of next month's ATP Montreal Masters, organizers Tennis Canada said Friday.In a packed schedule, world number one Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic both had deep runs at Wimbledon earlier this month, where Italian Sinner won the men's title and Serbian Djokovic reached the semi-finals.
fullText:
Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic have pulled out of next month's ATP Montreal Masters, organizers Tennis Canada said Friday.

In a packed schedule, world number one Sinner and 24-time Grand Slam champion Djokovic both had deep runs at Wimbledon earlier this month, where Italian Sinner won the men's title and Serbian Djokovic reached the semi-finals.

"After carefully considering all the factors together with my team, we have made the difficult decision to withdraw from Montreal," Sinner said in a statement.

"It is never easy to miss such an important event, but we believe this is the right decision to prioritize my health."

The Montreal men's event, which takes place August 1-13, is an ATP Masters 1000 tournament, and a key pre-US Open stopping point.

The parallel women's WTA 1000 tournament takes place this year in Toronto, with the two competitions switching between the cities on alternate years.

Organizers expressed disappointment at the last-minute withdrawals, noting that the two men also pulled out of last year's event in Toronto.

"We respect their decisions and understand that, with such a demanding schedule, players' health must remain the priority," tournament director Valerie Tetreault said in a statement.

"That said, we believe the frequency of these last-minute withdrawals in the last few years raises a broader issue for our sport."

"Masters 1000 events are among the flagship tournaments on the tour, and fans rightfully expect to see the world's best compete."

Tetreault said organizers are in discussions with the ATP over "adjustments" that are "needed in the near future to better protect the integrity of our Masters 1000 events while remaining mindful of the realities players face."

World number two Alexander Zverev -- this year's French Open champion and Wimbledon finalist -- is now expected to be the Montreal top seed, followed by Quebec native Felix Auger-Aliassime.

Third-ranked Spaniard Carlos Alcaraz had already withdrawn from Montreal over a lingering wrist injury.

He is targeting a return at the Cincinnati ATP Masters 1000 tournament, which begins immediately after Montreal.

The US Open, the year's final Grand Slam, starts on August 30 in New York.

title: Chelsea make opening offer for Bayer Leverkusen prodigy
description: Bayer Leverkusen have received a first offer from Chelsea for Kerim Alajbegovic, according to Kicker.The German publication reports that the Blues are prepared to pay more than €30 million for the 1...
fullText:
Bayer Leverkusen have received a first offer from Chelsea for Kerim Alajbegovic, according to Kicker.

The German publication reports that the Blues are prepared to pay more than €30 million for the 18-year-old attacker.

Die Werkself, meanwhile, are understood to be holding out for a total package worth €40 million for Alajbegovic.

Chelsea have yet to reach an agreement with Alajbegovic, with talks between the club and the Bosnia and Herzegovina youth international still to begin.

Leverkusen sold the youngster to RB Salzburg last summer, but later decided to re-sign him by activating a buy-back clause worth around €8 million.

Alajbegovic has been primarily linked with Atalanta this summer, but negotiations over the transfer fee between the Italian side and Leverkusen have proven difficult. Things appear to be progressing more smoothly with Chelsea in that regard.

fullText:

Last season, the Gators had eight players on the preseason All-SEC teams, many of whom are now in the NFL, such as Jake Slaughter, Caleb Banks, and Austin Barber.

title: Arsenal is facing massive competition for coveted winger
description: Arsenal are interested in signing Yan Diomande after the Ivorian’s proposed move to Paris Saint-Germain reportedly stalled, raising the possibility that the transfer could collapse. However, the Gun...
fullText:
Arsenal are interested in signing Yan Diomande after the Ivorian’s proposed move to Paris Saint-Germain reportedly stalled, raising the possibility that the transfer could collapse. However, the Gunners are not the only club monitoring the situation, with several European giants ready to compete for his signature this summer.

Diomande has established himself as one of Europe’s most promising young attackers since last year and earned selection for the Ivory Coast national team at the most recent World Cup. His impressive performances have enhanced his reputation and attracted significant interest from leading clubs across the continent.

Diomande’s outstanding form at RB Leipzig prompted Liverpool to submit a substantial offer for the forward before the World Cup. However, the German club rejected the approach and insisted that the player was not available for transfer, underlining their desire to retain one of their brightest talents.

In the weeks that followed, Diomande reportedly decided that he wanted to join Paris Saint-Germain after the French champions expressed an interest in signing him. Despite that development, the proposed transfer has failed to make significant progress, leaving his future uncertain ahead of the new season.

According to Goal, Arsenal are now looking to hijack the move, but they face competition from Manchester City and Real Madrid, both of whom remain interested in signing the attacker. If it becomes clear that a move to Paris Saint-Germain will not be completed, all three clubs are expected to step up their pursuit.

The increased competition could make Arsenal’s task considerably more difficult as they attempt to secure one of Europe’s most highly rated young forwards. London is widely regarded as an attractive destination for footballers, and Diomande could view a move to the English capital as an appealing alternative if the proposed transfer to Paris Saint-Germain ultimately falls through.

title: Chelsea make final decision on forward’s future amid exit rumours
description: Pedro Neto transfer latest as Chelsea keep winger despite growing competitionChelsea’s summer has already developed the dense, layered feel of a squad being reshaped in real time, and Pedro Neto now...
fullText:
Chelsea’s summer has already developed the dense, layered feel of a squad being reshaped in real time, and Pedro Neto now sits near the centre of that intrigue. According to Standard Sport, Chelsea “are not actively looking to sell Pedro Neto”, a line that offers clarity amid a market quick to confuse opportunity with intent.

That distinction matters. In modern squad building, a club can be open to movement without seeking it. The report states that there are “no immediate plans to sell the Portuguese winger despite rumours of an exit”, and, crucially, “no clubs have entered into anything close to serious talks with the Blues over signing Neto.” For now, that places the conversation in the realm of theory rather than negotiation.

The speculation has grown in part because Chelsea have committed £117million to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa. That fee alone ensures attention, and it naturally raises questions over minutes, roles and hierarchy. Rogers is expected to take significant time in Neto’s preferred area, the left side, a space already under pressure from Jamie Gittens and the broader flexibility within the squad.

There was also a claim that Tottenham had asked about Neto, though that has been challenged. As the report notes, “There was a report last week that Tottenham had enquired about Neto’s availability, but this has been disputed by sources at both clubs.”

Neto’s own season explains why this story has traction. He “played 46 times in all competitions last term, scoring six goals”, a solid body of work, though one that never quite translated into permanence. He “struggled to cement himself as a regular starter amid inconsistent form”, and that line captures the issue neatly. At elite clubs, availability is useful, certainty is priceless.

Chelsea’s options now seem abundant to the point of congestion. Neto can work from either flank, Estevao carries his own excitement, while Rogers and Cole Palmer offer further tactical elasticity. The report adds that “it remains to be seen what shape new manager Xabi Alonso will opt to plump for”, and that may be the essential point. Neto’s future may depend less on transfer interest and more on the geometry of Chelsea’s next idea.

From a Chelsea fan’s point of view, this all feels fairly straightforward. Neto is a good player, he works hard, and there is clearly talent there, so there is no real reason for the club to push him out the door. If Chelsea “are not actively looking to sell Pedro Neto”, that sounds sensible enough. Not every squad decision has to become a dramatic transfer saga.

The bigger issue is competition. Chelsea have loaded this squad with wide players and hybrid attackers, so naturally somebody is going to lose minutes. That does not automatically mean Neto has failed, it simply means he has to respond. If he “struggled to cement himself as a regular starter amid inconsistent form”, then this season becomes a test of personality as much as quality.

Supporters will probably accept that Chelsea “would listen to serious offers for Neto but have no plans to sell him”, because that is just how top clubs operate now. Everyone has a price, but that is different from wanting a player gone.

There is still a useful role for Neto, especially across a long season with injuries, rotation and tactical tweaks. He offers directness, speed and variation, and those things matter. The key for him is to make himself impossible to ignore. If he does that, the depth chart changes quickly. If he does not, the rumours will return, louder than before.

title: Real Madrid working to sign Manchester City midfield general with renewal talks not progressing
description: In a major development, David Ornstein of The Athletic reports that Real Madrid have launched an operation to sign Manchester City’s midfield anchor Rodri, dramatically shifting their summer transfe...
fullText:
In a major development, David Ornstein of The Athletic reports that Real Madrid have launched an operation to sign Manchester City’s midfield anchor Rodri, dramatically shifting their summer transfer strategy to secure the newly crowned World Cup winner.

Formal club-to-club negotiations between the Spanish heavyweights and the Premier League giants have yet to officially take place.

But those at Valdebebas are growing increasingly confident that a definitive agreement can be reached.

The board is currently operating under the firm assumption that the Spain international will be joining the club before the conclusion of the summer window.

The sudden pursuit represents a total reversal of Madrid’s previous market planning.

Throughout the early months of the summer, sources at the Bernabeu repeatedly insisted that Rodri was not part of their recruitment strategy.

However, the club’s stance completely transformed following the midfielder’s return from the FIFA World Cup in North America.

Real Madrid step up Rodri pursuit. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Rodri’s unparalleled performance levels and his pivotal role in captaining Luis de la Fuente’s side to back-to-back major tournament trophies heavily influenced Florentino Perez’s decision to sanction a move.

Starting and captaining his country across all eight matches, his exceptional tournament culminated in him lifting the prestigious Golden Ball after Spain defeated Argentina in a dramatic final.

For Manchester City, the situation represents an escalating crisis during a period of massive structural transition.

New manager Enzo Maresca remains determined to keep the 30-year-old at the heart of his tactical plans for the upcoming 2026-27 campaign, and City executives remain in active dialogue with the player’s camp over his long-term future.

However, their leverage is rapidly diminishing. Rodri has officially entered the final 12 months of his contract, which runs until June 2027.

No interest in renewing his contract. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images)

Despite City’s persistent efforts to schedule high-level extension talks immediately after the World Cup, the player has so far shown little to no desire to renew his deal in England.

The move to the Bernabeu aligns perfectly with Rodri’s long-standing personal and professional ambitions.

The midfield general has frequently spoken about his profound desire to return to his home country before the end of his playing career, openly acknowledging the unique prestige associated with wearing the white shirt.

“Would I like to play in Spain again, in La Liga, in Madrid? I would like to return, yes, obviously,” Rodri candidly told reporters during the March international break.

While a looming surgery to resolve a persistent back issue adds a layer of medical complication regarding his exact return date, Real Madrid remain undeterred, viewing the midfielder as the ultimate Galactico signing to solidify their team.

title: 'We wanted to be Bournemouth' - Rose begins Cherries reign with win
description: Marco Rose kicked off his Bournemouth reign with a 4-1 victory over German side St. Pauli in the Cherries' opening pre-season fixture.  Rose's side fell a goal behind in the first half, but goals from Ben Gannon-Doak, Harold William, Daniel Jebbison and Bafode Diakite helped Bournemouth seal a victory in Saalfelden, Austria.  Speaking to BBC Radio Solent, the Cherries boss said he was "pleased" with the result and that he was content with the performance from his players.
fullText:
Marco Rose kicked off his Bournemouth reign with a 4-1 victory over German side St. Pauli in the Cherries' opening pre-season fixture.

Rose's side fell a goal behind in the first half, but goals from Ben Gannon-Doak, Harold William, Daniel Jebbison and Bafode Diakite helped Bournemouth seal a victory in Saalfelden, Austria.

Speaking to BBC Radio Solent, the Cherries boss said he was "pleased" with the result and that he was content with the performance from his players.

"I saw many good things, but it is good to have a first game with footage and work on things that we need to improve.

"We wanted to be Bournemouth, and we wanted to be proactive, and I think that is what we saw today," said Rose.

Alex Scott, who has been linked with a move away from Bournemouth, featured, but Eli Junior Kroupi did not play due to a lack of training.

When asked about the speculation which surrounds Scott and Kroupi, Rose said: "I am not here to comment on any rumours or things like this."

Although Rose declined to comment on potential outgoings at Bournemouth, he said it was "not a secret" that the south coast side are aiming to sign defender, Antonio Silva from Benfica.

"We want this player, the player wants to join us and the clubs are in talks – that's nothing new. Now we are waiting for him," added Rose.

title: How To Watch WNBA All-Star 2026, Schedule & Streaming Info
description: How to watch WNBA All-Star 2026: Get the full schedule, events, TV channels, streaming details, Shooting Stars contest and All-Star Game information.
fullText:
WNBA All-Star Weekend has become one of the most anticipated events on the women’s sports calendar, bringing together the league’s biggest stars, rising talent, brand partners, and a growing global audience.

As fans prepare to watch the 2026 festivities, here's everything to know about the schedule, events, broadcast information, and how to stream every moment.

This year instead of a traditional skills challenge, the WNBA is premiering the Shooting Stars four team contest. The four teams will be anchored by WNBA alumni and legends.

Two-time Kia WNBA MVP and Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame Class of 2026 member Elena Delle Donne, three-time Kia WNBA Most Valuable Player and Naismith Hall of Famer Lauren Jackson, five-time WNBA champion Rebekkah Brunson and three-time WNBA champion Deanna “Tweety” Nolan will headline the field for the Kia WNBA Shooting Stars.

The Kia WNBA Shooting Stars will feature four teams representing the WNBA’s Minnesota, Seattle, Washington and Dallas/Detroit markets.

Joining the WNBA legends are 2026 WNBA All-Stars Jessica Shepard of the Dallas Wings and Courtney Williams of the Minnesota Lynx, along with 2022 All-Rookie Team selection Shakira Austin of the Washington Mystics and standout 2026 rookie Flau’jae Johnson of the Seattle Storm.

Each team will also include a standout high school player from the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL). Jezelle “GG” Banks, Ryan Carter, Tatianna Griffin and Morghan Reckley will represent Nike EYBL.

The Kia WNBA Shooting Stars is a two-round, timed shooting competition in which teams have 70 seconds to score as many points as possible from seven shooting locations around the court. The two teams posting the highest scores in the opening round advancing to the championship round.

The Kia WNBA Shooting Stars and Three-Point Contest competitions will be broadcast from Wintrust Arena, home of the Chicago Sky, on Friday, July 24 at 8 p.m. ET. The contest will be on ESPN as well as made available with the fubo, Disney+, and ESPN App streaming platforms.

The WNBA All-Star Three-Point Contest made news this week as Caitlin Clark, Kayla McBride, and reigning champion Sabrina Ionescu were reported to have declined the offer to participate and compete. However, Ionescu has since called out the claim as inaccurate, indicating she was never invited to participate.

Despite Ionescu, Clark, and McBride’s absence from the contest, the field includes other sharp shooters in the Atlanta Dream’s Rhyne Howard, Toronto Tempo’s Mabrina Mabrey, Portland Fire’s Bridget Carleton, Golden State Valkyries Janelle Salaün, and Storm’s Natasha Hiedman.

Fan favorite and No. 1 rookie draft pick Azzi Fudd of the Dallas Wings will also compete for the first time.

On Saturday, July 25 at 8:30 pm EST on ABC and also streaming on ESPN, fubo, and the ESPN app, the two All-Star teams led by general managers and WNBA legends Cynthia Cooper and Teresa Weatherspoon will face off.

The contest will take place at United Center, a massive move and upgrade for the WNBA All-Star game. The two teams are coached by four-time WNBA champion Cheryl Reeve and three-time WNBA champion Becky Hammon.

title: 3 unanswered questions before training camp: Denver Broncos edition
description: The Broncos' offense still belongs to head coach Sean Payton, but what can be injected now that Davis Webb is taking over play-calling?
fullText:
As we work our way through our last NFL division for our "3 unanswered questions" series, we take a look at the AFC West and the Denver Broncos. Broncos coach Sean Payton has been an offense-minded play-caller for almost 20 years and handed off those duties to fast-rising offensive coach Davis Webb. Why? To keep him around. He wanted to inject some creativity and unpredictability into the offense. Will it work? Or will the defense overshadow them?

With the arrival of Jaylen Waddle, the Broncos appear to be better on paper than last year, but the game isn't played on paper now, is it? Denver has a demanding schedule this season, including games against the NFC West. Could they take a step backward from the level of play last year with a mostly healthy Bo Nix?

The Broncos' offense still belongs to head coach Sean Payton, but what can be injected now that Davis Webb is taking over play-calling? Fans want to see Webb lean into the areas where Bo Nix thrives: up-tempo, no-huddle drives. If the Broncos lean into that, they may find themselves right back into the thick of things.

The Broncos will look to spread the ball around more, especially in the backfield, this year. How it will be divided up remains to be seen. Payton knows that it can be difficult to get three backs involved with adequate work, but Jonah Coleman's pass protection ability could earn him a third-down role on offense.

fullText:

Meanwhile, a trio of Sixers players -- Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid and the newly acquired Jaylen Brown, another surprising addition for Philadelphia this offseason -- worked on James directly, sources told ESPN. That effort was led by Maxey, a fellow Klutch client who has referred to James as a "big brother" in the past. — 7/24/2026 ESPN

Grant Hill: 'Contrary to popular belief, I do like Jaylen Brown. I love his game, and things got difficult there with that team. In putting the team together, just to give some context, we had Kawhi Leonard on that penciled in on that team, and he got hurt at the end of that season in 2024. Joel Embiid was, you know, we knew we were managing him, but we needed him for Nikola Jokic against Serbia, because that was the matchup. title: Angel Reese opens up about Barack Obama selfie, new Barbie doll
description: Angel Reese met Barack Obama at WNBA All-Star Weekend in Chicago, and debuted her new signature Barbie doll.
fullText:
CHICAGO — When Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese landed back in Chicago for 2026 WNBA All-Star Weekend on Thursday, July 23, it took a little longer for her to deplane.

A special VIP landed at the same time.

"When my plane was landing yesterday ... they said, 'VIP. Nobody can get off the plane,'" Reese recalled on Friday, July 24. "I'm like, 'Well, we're VIP too.' And then they said, 'Obama.' And I was like, 'OK, OK, OK.'”

REQUIRED READING: Caitlin Clark bonds with Barack Obama at WNBA All-Star weekend over media scrutiny

The special VIP was former President Barack Obama, who surprised the WNBA All-Stars at the eponymous Barack Obama Presidential Center early July 24. Obama gave a brief speech during team practice, shook everyone's hand and even played "one on one" with Jonquel Jones. He also posed for photos, an opportunity Reese described as once-in-a-lifetime.

"Not everybody just gets to meet Barack (Obama). That was my first time too," added Reese, who took pictures of her teammates with the former president. "Baby, you got to get your (picture). I'm getting a picture of everybody. I got one of (Kahleah Copper), got one of me, a selfie. I think it's important just to capture every moment."

Everyone needs a friend like Angel Reese 📸😂

President Obama had the All-Stars hyped before they became the first to hit the court at the Obama Presidential Center! pic.twitter.com/Jp4s0LkKc6

Reese previously appeared on former first lady Michelle Obama's podcast in April, which she hosts alongside her brother Craig Robinson. The trio discussed everything from mental health to navigating fame.

"Michelle (Obama) made me feel the empowerment of what a woman is like to go through so many different things," Reese said. "To be in front of the world and have your back against the wall and just be able to go against all the odds and everything that she was doing. And she gave me a lot of advice. So I appreciate Michelle (Obama) and she pours so much into me and I'm just really happy."

Reese began her career in Chicago after being drafted No. 7 overall by the Chicago Sky in 2024. She was traded to the Atlanta Dream ahead of the 2026 WNBA season and said it "feels really good" to be back in the Windy City.

"I'm really happy to be back here and it gives me déjà vu from when I was here my rookie year and last year," Reese said, adding that she's still tapped into the Chicago community. "To be here at the Obama Center and know what it means. My foundation is actually working with the Obamas and doing some things in the community as well. My mom went to their event a couple weeks ago, so it's really cool. Being able to see the community grow, our pictures on the billboards is really cool."

As Reese spoke with reporters during her WNBA All-Star media availability, there was another special guest making its rounds around the room: her new signature Barbie Doll.

Reese has been nicknamed the Bayou Barbie since playing at LSU, where she brought the program its first national championship in 2023. She debuted her new doll at WNBA All-Star Weekend — a full-circle moment for the three-time All-Star.

"I really wanted to have a Barbie doll one day and to have a Barbie, you got to be iconic. You have to do some real things," Reese said on Friday. "I knew it was going to take some time because there's so many great women that are Barbie dolls and they have their own doll, but I knew that's what I wanted. And I spoke that into existence."

title: Jenny Shin leads the Women's Scottish Open by 5 strokes after two rounds
description: South Korea’s Jenny Shin led the Women's Scottish Open by five strokes after two rounds at Dundonald Links on Friday.  Shin started the second round with a bogey and shrugged it off with six birdies, including on her final hole, for a 5-under 67.  Shin was co-leader with American Lauren Coughlin on 6 under after day one of the tournament co-sanctioned by the Ladies European Tour and LPGA Tour.
fullText:
TROON, Scotland (AP) — South Korea’s Jenny Shin led the Women's Scottish Open by five strokes after two rounds at Dundonald Links on Friday.

Shin started the second round with a bogey and shrugged it off with six birdies, including on her final hole, for a 5-under 67. She's at 11 under overall.

Shin was co-leader with American Lauren Coughlin on 6 under after day one of the tournament co-sanctioned by the Ladies European Tour and LPGA Tour. But Coughlin, who won the Aramco Championship in April and the Scottish Open in 2024, hit 2 over on Friday and dropped to 4 under and a tie for fourth with Japan’s Erika Hara.

The closest to Shin was German golfer Esther Henseleit, who carded 4-under 68 with two birdies and an eagle.

South Korea's A Lim Kim remained at 5 under and in third place after an even par round with two birdies and two bogeys.

Sweden's Anna Nordqvist shot 7 over to drop from a tie for fifth to just above the cut line on 5 over.

title: Ohio State Makes Early Move on 2029 Basketball Standout
description: Ohio State has offered 2029 standout Noah Woods, adding an early Big Ten suitor to the rising recruit’s growing list.
fullText:
It's never too early to make an early impression, and Ohio State head coach Jake Diebler is trying to do just that by making an offer on a 2029 prospect.

Noah Woods said on his social media that he had a "wonderful" conversation with the head coach and received a scholarship offer from the University. Woods is a 6-foot-9, 200-pound forward out of Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Big Ten Rivals Iowa and Nebraska have also offered, along with the home-state school South Dakota.

According to Nick Osen, a reporter from 24/7 sports, "Woods really impressed me. He is one of my biggest stock risers of the weekend, and I will be very intrigued to see where he is ranked in the class of 2029. A 6-foot-8-plus combo forward as I like to call it, he legitimately has some guard skillsets in terms of handles, vision and passing while still being able to defend and play above the rim. It is not hyperbole that he is a top 30 kid in his class, while some I trust believe he could end up even higher."

Woods becomes the third player in the 2029 recruiting cycle to receive an offer from Ohio State. The Buckeyes are also pursuing Bryce Irby and Mason Grivna.

Ohio State's strategy seems simple. If a program makes an evaluation and finds a prospect it likes, being one of the first to make an offer and starting the relationship early can potentially be a deciding factor when the prospect is ready to make a decision.

title: CBS analyst Tony Romo reportedly arrested in Milwaukee for suspicion of operating while intoxicated
description: Tony Romo is reportedly due back in court in September.
fullText:
Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback — and current CBS analyst — Tony Romo was reportedly arrested Thursday for suspicion of operating while intoxicated (OWI), per FOX6 News in Wisconsin.

Romo, 46, was reportedly arrested by the Milwaukee County Sheriff's Office while driving on a highway in the city. An arrest detention report obtained by FOX6 News claimed Romo was taken into custody after performing poorly when given a field-sobriety test.

Romo was reportedly booked and released and due back in court Sept. 21.

A first offense charge or OWI carries a fine and a temporary driver's license suspension in Wisconsin. Depending on Romo's blood-alcohol level, he could also be subject to a year in a sobriety program.

It's unclear whether the arrest will affect Romo's employment with CBS. If that court date holds, it would take place on a Monday during the NFL season. Romo typically works on Sundays during the NFL regular season.

Romo, who grew up and went to high school in Wisconsin, attended Eastern Illinois before he was signed as an undrafted free agent by the Cowboys in 2003.

He worked his way onto the 53-man roster and eventually claimed a starting role three years later. Romo impressed immediately in his first opportunity as a starter, tossing 19 touchdowns against 13 interceptions in 10 starts and making the Pro Bowl.

Over his 13-year career, all of which came with the Cowboys, Romo threw 248 touchdowns. He made four Pro Bowls and one All-Pro second team during his career.

Upon retiring from the NFL, Romo began working as the lead color commentator for CBS, where he's frequently paired up with Jim Nantz to call games, including Super Bowl LVIII.

title: Where former Oregon PG Payton Pritchard lands in redo of 2020 NBA Draft
description: Payton Pritchard has far outperformed his No. 26 overall draft spot, but just how far does he rise in a 2020 NBA redraft?
fullText:
During Payton Pritchard's first four seasons in the NBA, he was largely used as an end-of-the-bench reserve for the Boston Celtics. As the 26th pick in the first round in the 2020 NBA Draft after four seasons with the Oregon Ducks, he had slightly begun to live up to the late-first-round billing in Year 4, averaging 9.6 points for a Celtics team that won the title.

But the rise continued into the 2024-25 season when point guard Jrue Holiday was traded away, clearing a prominent bench role for the former Duck. Pritchard averaged 14.3 points and 3.5 assists while converting on 40.7% of his triples, winning the NBA's Sixth Man of the Year award.

Now coming off a season in which he started 50 games for Boston and averaged a career-high 17.0 points and 5.2 assists, it's clear that Pritchard has far outpaced his 26th overall spot in the 2020 draft.

But just how far up would he go in a 2020 redraft?

According to The Ringer's Bill Simmons, Pritchard would go 10th overall, only behind stars such as Anthony Edwards, Tyrese Haliburton, Tyrese Maxey and several others.

"Pritchard took a couple years," Simmons said during an episode of The Bill Simmons Podcast. "I always liked him more than it seemed like the coaches liked him and it was always unclear why he wasn't getting the car keys a little bit more, and I think the team liked him because they gave him a contract even before he'd kind of become who he became. And then he just became one of the best bench guards in the league. Last year, he moved into a whole different level."

Heading into the 2026-27 season, Pritchard has a chance to move up yet another level. The Celtics traded away last years leading scorer Jaylen Brown, who took 21.7 shots per night. While Jayson Tatum and Paul George, who arrived via the Brown trade, will take some of those looks, the door is cracked open even more for an increased amount of Pritchard shots.

Already, Pritchard is making teams with picks in the 10's and early 20's of the 2020 draft wish they could've taken him, but that regret could reach an even higher mark in the seasons to come.

title: Journalist: Liverpool ‘interested’ in move for forward with £77m release clause
description: Liverpool Transfer News: Reds to Reignite Their Interest in La Liga ForwardMost of the latest transfer news around Liverpool has become a bit repetitive, and a familiar name has surfaced once again.Wo...
fullText:
Most of the latest transfer news around Liverpool has become a bit repetitive, and a familiar name has surfaced once again.

World Cup winner Nico Williams is reportedly on Liverpool’s shortlist again as they continue their search to replace Mohamed Salah.

PSG forward Bradley Barcola remains the priority it seems, but a move for Williams could be on the cards.

The Athletic Bilbao forward has been tipped for a major move for a couple of years now, and he might finally get his wish.

According to Ekrem Konur, Liverpool are once again interested in a potential move for the 24-year-old forward. However, they aren’t currently leading the race for his signature…

Speaking on X, he said: “Liverpool are interested in Nico Williams, but Arsenal’s pursuit is currently more advanced.”

“Arsenal have made new contacts for the Athletic Club winger, with sporting director Andrea Berta assessing whether a deal is feasible.”

“His contract includes a £77m release clause, a figure Arsenal and several Premier League clubs can realistically meet.”

At one point Williams was one of the hottest prospects in Europe. Last summer he was on the verge of signing for Barcelona, before agreeing a shock ten year contract to keep him at the club until 2035.

But it’s important to note that the contract included a £77m release clause.

Going back to 2023/24, Williams shone for Athletic Club with 18 direct goal involvements in 31 league appearances. He then was a standout performer for Spain in their EURO 2024 triumph.

However, since then he has only managed ten goal involvements in his last two league campaigns (5 goals, 5 assists in 24/25 + 6 goals, 4 assists in 25/26).

He has never managed to score more than 11 goals across all competitions in a single season so far. So it’s arguable whether there is true value in his £77m release clause.

But the potential is clearly there. Electric pace, quick feet but not quite the end product that Liverpool need after the departure of Mohamed Salah, who still managed 12 goals and 10 assists last season.

title: Budda Baker shows support as Jacoby Brissett practices in training camp
description: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett reported to training camp, practiced and Budda Baker was supportive.
fullText:
After a lot of huffing and puffing over the last three months and loads of incessant chatter and opinions, Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett reported for training camp Wednesday with the remainder of the team and then participated in Thursday’s first practice of the summer.

It’s been known since early April that Brissett wants a raise from his scheduled $4.88 million in salary for 2026 that includes $1.5 million that is guaranteed. Since Day 1, the Cardinals have been negotiating with Brissett, but as camp opened, there has not been a meeting of the minds for what that improved deal would look like.

Addressing the media prior to practice Thursday, head coach Mike LaFleur said Brissett would be on the field and that talks were “still ongoing” while adding they have been “productive.”

When asked if there is a quarterback competition, if Brissett would practice with the first team and how he would “describe” it, LaFleur said, “I'd describe it as practice one on July 23rd.”

As for any other details, LaFleur said, “I'm not even going to get into all those specifics,” while noting that Brissett had no reps in the new offensive scheme during offseason workouts.

“It’s just getting him up to speed with our operation, with our cadence, with our formations, our no-huddle package, our pass game, our run game, all that kind of stuff,” he said. “So, not really worried about that stuff right now. Really not worried about what any of these guys have ever done in the past. It's just about building it one day at a time and seeing how good we can be every single day.”

In early July, Cardinals safety Budda Baker posted on social media about the situation, writing, “Just want bro to get his (expletive) done. He is not asking for what you think. Bro is asking for below the bare minimum. Let’s just get it done!!!”

When Baker spoke to the media after LaFleur on Thursday, he said he wasn’t aware that Brisset would be practicing when many wondered if he would report and then “hold in.” Not reporting would have meant daily fines of $60,000 as well as fines for missing preseason games at over $287,000 for each one.

“That’s a great thing,” Baker said of the news Brissett would practice. “I want all of our players to get theirs and ultimately all of our players to be in the building and being able to practice, being able to get better because you only get better by practicing. Definitely excited for not only Jacoby, but all the quarterbacks to come in, first week of training camp, get their feet wet, and continue to get better.”

When it was mentioned that he’s usually careful about what he posts on social media, he was asked if the tweet was done out of frustration or if it was with the knowledge that camp was opening soon.

He said, “Getting closer to the start of camp. At the end of the day, I want the best guys to be on the field. And I don't know if it's competition or not competition, but just to have as many players that we can have to compete for a role, that's definitely special for me. Because that's how you get better. That's how you win games is by competing.

“Just getting towards camp, I'm getting a little itchy and some things were slightly said. That's just how I am. I just want everyone to be on the field. If you're signed with the Arizona Cardinals, be on the field, get work in, grind, take it one day at a time, and whoever's with the ones is with the ones. But at the end of the day, you're only going to get better by practicing. So, just the ability to have him even practicing, that's going to be good for him because he hasn't practiced at all.

Baker then joked, “Hopefully he's with the ones so I can pick him off. You know, I'm just a competitor at heart.”

Get more Cardinals and NFL coverage from Cards Wire's Jess Root and others by listening to the latest on the Rise Up, See Red podcast. Subscribe on Spotify, YouTube or Apple Podcasts.

title: The TaylorMade putter Michael Kim used to shoot a 59
description: Learn about the club Michael Kim used on the 18th hole at the 3M Open to card the 16th sub-60 round in PGA Tour history.
fullText:
When Michael Kim's third shot to the par-5 18th hole at TPC Twin Cities on Friday hit the green and peeled back to just over 24 feet from the hole, there was a collective disappointment in the crowd. The shot was nothing to turn your nose up at, but from that distance, Kim was unlikely to hole the birdie putt, and a birdie would give the 33-year-old former University of California standout a 59.

But after sizing up the putt, Kim knocked it in the back of the hole to card the 16th sub-60 round in PGA Tour history and take the lead midway through the second round at the 3M Open in Blaine, Minnasota.

The putter that got the job done and helped Kim make an astonishing 11 birdies on Friday is a zero-torque TaylorMade Spider ZT Black, a dark version of the original TaylorMade Spider ZT.

Scottie Scheffler, Rory McIlroy and a host of other players use TaylorMade Spider Tour putters, but while the zero-torque version is popular at retail, not many pros are using it. The biggest difference is, of course, that the zero-torque version has a shaft that goes directly into the head above the center of gravity (CG) location, and that reduces the putter's propensity to rotate open or closed as you make your stroke. The result for many golfers is that it becomes easier to return the face back to square and get your putts started on your intended target line.

On Friday, Kim had a staggering Strokes Gained: Putting of +6.68 for round two, ranking first in the 143-man field. Kim also made over 145 feet of putts Friday.

The first golfer to win a major championship using a zero-torque putter came last season when J.J. Spaun won the U.S. Open at Oakmont using a L.A.B. DF3. Today, Kim became the first player to shoot a sub-60 round with one.

David Dusek is a senior writer at Golfweek covering golf equipment.

title: 76ers superstar LeBron James reportedly nearly retired from basketball after season with Lakers
description: LeBron James has finally made a decision as to where he will be playing the rest of his career. After announcing his decision, he made it clear that he almost didn't come back to basketball.
fullText:
76ers superstar LeBron James reportedly nearly retired from basketball after season with Lakers originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The entire LeBron James process has been a whirlwind, leaving many people in the dark due to the lack of information coming from the four-time NBA champion. James wanted to make this decision on his own terms and, most importantly, on his own timeline.

Throughout the process, James eventually revealed what he was looking for in his next team. He wanted to join an organization that embodied championship habits.

“What's most important is that I want to compete. I want to compete at a high level. I want to join a franchise that shares the same model as myself. That's like practicing championship habits every day,” James said.

After nearly an entire month of evaluating his options and going through his thought process, James decided to join an intriguing Philadelphia 76ers roster featuring Tyrese Maxey, Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, and VJ Edgecombe.

“LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers for his final run at another NBA championship, he announced Friday,” ESPN’s Dave McMenamin wrote. “James, 41, is signing a two-year, $8 million contract with a player option, Klutch Sports Group CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania.”

Now that James is off the board, the rest of the NBA free agents can decide where they want to continue their careers. However, the four-time NBA champion revealed that he thought his career was over after playing his final game with the Los Angeles Lakers.

“I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and decide if I still love,” James posted.

The 76ers landed the biggest name of the summer and are as excited as anyone. Their starting five could be the best in the league, but the team’s depth still needs improvement. Throughout his career, James has excelled when paired with younger players he can mentor and help develop.

Philadelphia was not even considered a serious contender at the start of free agency, but Boston’s decision to send Jaylen Brown to the 76ers changed everything. The next two years of James’ career in Philadelphia should be fascinating to watch.

title: Blackhawks hoping that Patrick Kane will ignite Chicago's weak offense for a second time
description: When the Chicago Blackhawks selected Patrick Kane No. 1 overall in the 2007 draft, they counted on the forward, then just 18, to give their rebuilding team and its sputtering offense an immediate boost.  Fast-forward 19 years: The Blackhawks again hope that Kane, now 37 and entering his 20th NHL season, will do the same after signing the all-time scoring leader among U.S.-born players to a $16 million, two-year deal.
fullText:
CHICAGO (AP) — When the Chicago Blackhawks selected Patrick Kane No. 1 overall in the 2007 draft, they counted on the forward, then just 18, to give their rebuilding team and its sputtering offense an immediate boost.

Fast-forward 19 years: The Blackhawks again hope that Kane, now 37 and entering his 20th NHL season, will do the same after signing the all-time scoring leader among U.S.-born players to a $16 million, two-year deal.

“I mean that’s kind of always what I’ve been known to do is help produce,” Kane said Friday at the Blackhawks practice facility. “I don’t think that’s going to change any time now. I’m excited to come back and try to produce and fit in with all these young players and guys that I can play with, help build chemistry, learn. So do all those things. Help the team win. Help the team score."

Kane said he feels strong three years after undergoing a major hip resurfacing surgery and rehabbing his way back for three solid seasons with the Detroit Red Wings.

Kane has 1,400 points in 1,369 career NHL games (508 goals and 892 assists). He cranked out 16 goals and 41 assists in 67 games last season for Detroit and says he’s not slowing down.

Kane had discussions with his hometown Buffalo Sabres after becoming a free agent on July 1. But it seems to have been an easy decision to return to Chicago, where he spent his first 15-plus NHL seasons and helped the Blackhawks win three Stanley Cup championships as one of the NHL’s most electrifying players.

Kane said there wasn’t one deciding factor in returning to Chicago, where he has spent his summers. He acknowledged the homecoming, but said his biggest focus is helping a team “that’s on the rise, a team that’s looking to make some big steps forward and trying to make the playoffs"

“It’s not like I’m just coming back home, to you know, ride off into the sunset or whatever it is," Kane said “You know I want to be a big player here and help the team win.”

Part of that will be meshing with Chicago’s young forwards. That starts with center Connor Bedard, the Blackhawks only other No. 1 overall draft pick who was selected in 2023.

Bedard will miss the early part of the season after left shoulder surgery on July 8. Bedard, who signed a $75 million, five-year contract last week, got hurt skating with a group of NHL players near his home in suburban Vancouver. Once Bedard returns, Kane can’t wait to skate with him.

“He’s such a special player,” Kane said. “This will be my 20th year in the league and I’ll probably see passes I’ve never seen before playing with him. But I mean, wherever I fit in, I fit in. No matter who it is, I’m going to try to make the most of it.”

The statistical symmetry between the Blackhawks in 2006-07, the season before Kane entered as a rookie, and last year’s team is stunning.

The 2006-07 Blackhawks scored just 201 goals, second lowest in the NHL, as they went 31-42-9 for 71 points. With Kane in the lineup the following year — and posting 21 goals and 51 assists — Chicago jumped to 40-34-9 and 88 points. The Blackhawks scored 239 times and narrowly missed the playoffs.

In 2025-26, Chicago finished at 29-39-14 with 72 points, and scored just 213 goals, behind only Calgary (212).

Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson said it was time to bring Kane back after dealing him to the New York Rangers just before the March 2023 trade deadline.

Davidson was beginning a major overhaul of his roster then. In addition to focusing on prospects, he said the Blackhawks also needed to focus on building a new leadership core.

That process, with Bedard leading the way, has already started, Davidson said. Kane can only help now.

“They (Blackhawks young players) already know their way around the league a little bit,” Davidson said. “It’s the right time for him (Kane) to come, step in, join a group of of not all young players –- but a considerable group of young players -– and provide high-end play, but also high-end leadership and a lot of different things that he can impart on our young players."

title: Mark Pope gives update on filling Kentucky’s 15th roster spot
description: Pope has several avenues to work with to fill that final spot.
fullText:
It may be July, but there are still plenty of options for Kentucky Basketball to fill that 15th and final roster spot.

This is typically the time of the year when we see reclassifications happen now that the bulk of the summer AAU season is complete. International recruiting is another avenue Kentucky has landed several players from since Mark Pope arrived in Lexington.

And we can’t forget the emergence of fifth-year seniors who were set to have their eligibility expire but are now getting one more year thanks to ongoing lawsuits.

All of this is to say Kentucky still has time to add one more guy, and Pope discussed just that during his Friday meeting with local media.

“We have a spot open, and so we’re actively, every day, in conversations with everything from international guys, reclass guys, still transfer portal guys, and then of course this looming fifth-year eligibility, which would bring a huge influx of talent into the recruitable pool right now,” Pope told reporters. “Some guys that could be game-changers.”

The most recent big-name player to be granted a fifth year of eligibility is Auburn forward Keyshawn Hall, who averaged 19.3 points and 7.1 rebounds per game last season.

Other notable players who could gain one more season of eligibility if their lawsuits are successful include Michigan State forward Jaxon Kohler, UCLA point guard Donovan Dent, Texas guard Jordan Pope, UCLA guard Skyy Clark, and UC Santa Barbara guard Aidan Mahaney.

Will he manage to get it filled? With the start of the fall semester looming, we won’t have to wait long to find out.

title: ‘How is Supporting Caitlin Clark Racist?’ GOP Activist Slams ‘Insane’ USA Today Column Suggesting Fans of WNBA Star are White Nationalists
description: CJ Pearson suggested Nancy Armour's USA Today column bizarrely linking WNBA star Caitlin Clark to a racist 1955 murder was so atrocious she must have been drunk
fullText:
Conservative activist CJ Pearson suggested USA Today columnist Nancy Armour’s column bizarrely linking WNBA star Caitlin Clark to a racist 1955 murder and claiming a large chunk of her fans are white nationalists was so atrocious she must have been drunk when she wrote it.

Pearson slammed Armour’s much-maligned article during a Friday interview on The Faulkner Focus.

“It’s absolutely insane,” he said when asked for his reaction. “And I know it’s National Tequila Day, but it seems she got a head start in celebrating while writing this piece.”

He referred to a few sections which went extra-viral from the Wednesday piece.

Armour wrote Clark’s “flopping” was a big problem because it was putting other players in “danger.”

“It shouldn’t need reminding this country has an awful history of Black people being harmed, even killed, in the name of ‘defending’ white women,” Armour wrote. “The irony of the WNBA’s All-Star Game is that it’s happening this weekend in Chicago, the hometown of Emmett Till, who became an icon of the civil rights movement after his tragic murder.”

She added, “It seems there is a white nationalist faction to Clark’s fandom that is deeply, deeply problematic, made even more so because the WNBA is made up predominantly of Black women, many of them queer. When Clark claims fouls that don’t exist, when she goes on profanity-laced tirades at referees, those racists see her as a white woman in need of saving and take matters into their own hands.”

Pearson told Harris Faulkner the article didn’t make a lick of sense.

“How is supporting Caitlin Clark racist? How is in any way the treatment that she suffered at all in the neighborhood of comparison to the tragedy that happened to Emmett Till?” he asked. “These people are grasping for straws and absolutely, coming up short every single time.”

Armour admitted on Thursday she made an “inartful comparison” by bringing up Till, but doubled down on the overall slant of her story.

Pearson — who has been the co-chair of the Republican National Committee’s Youth Advisory Council since 2022 — added the coverage of Clark has been “a shame,” considering how great she has been for the WNBA.

title: Why LeBron's new team — the 76ers! — should happily trade for Bronny James
description: If LeBron wants to continue playing with his son in the NBA, it should be a no-brainer for the 76ers.
fullText:
At long last, LeBron James has made his decision. The 41-year-old is a Sixer, signing a two-year deal worth $8 million to join Philadelphia.

For James' free agency, it's not clear what the exact terms of engagement were during this round. But unlike past courtships, the employment status of James' son Bronny will likely be part of internal discussions with LeBron's new team in Philly. In 2024, when James' Los Angeles Lakers selected Bronny with the 55th pick in the draft, the Jameses became the first father-son pairing to play in the NBA together.

LeBron has not publicly stated that he'd like his eldest son to join him, and it's not a given the Lakers would satisfy any such request. But it also wouldn't be a surprise to hear that LeBron would prefer to continue playing with his son. In the playoffs, after throwing an alley-oop to Bronny in a Game 3 win over the Houston Rockets, LeBron didn't hold back his joy.

"It just keeps getting better and better," he said after the game. "It's like, wow."

As of now, there is no plan or request for Bronny to join his father, per ESPN Ramona Shelburne. But that could always change as the season draws closer. Bronny for the time being remains on the Lakers' roster, set to play his third year on a four-year contract that he signed in 2024. The 21-year-old became a rotation player by the end of last season, garnering 16.9 minutes per game while appearing in eight playoff games with the Lakers.

But president Bob Myers and the Philadelphia 76ers should happily acquire Bronny. Here are three reasons why.

Is Bronny James a good NBA player? I don't think anyone would argue that he is right now. The better framework is to count him among the hundred or so players who are trying to make it in the league. In 556 minutes over two seasons, he's averaging 2.7 points, 1.1 assists and 0.6 rebounds. Not great. On a per-minute basis, his career PER of 8.4 is 464th among 485 players with at least 500 minutes over the last two seasons. Still: not great.

But he's trending upward. The swing skill for Bronny is his 3-point shot, which would allow him to level up his athleticism with a perimeter threat. Last season, he made 22 of his 57 3-point shots, giving him a promising 38.6% conversion rate, an improvement from his debut mark of 28.1%. If he can maintain a strong percentage and continue to deliver strong on-ball defense, he'll be able to carve out a role as an NBA player.

There's also G-League data. In his age-20 and age-21 seasons, his G-League ledger shows that there's something there. In 25 career games in the G-League, Bronny is averaging 18.4 points, 4.4 assists and 4.0 rebounds in 30 minutes per game while shooting 49.6% from the floor, 41.3% on six 3-pointers per game and 80.5% from the line. For a defensive-minded player like Bronny, scoring 22 points per 36 minutes with an above-average 63.9% true shooting percentage at the G-League suggests he's more than ready for NBA minutes.

Maybe Bronny doesn't pan out to be a Top 300 player one day. Gary Payton II bounced around the league before he found a real home in Golden State at age 29. Bronny is eight years younger than GP2 and, despite his youth, teams will have hundreds of millions of reasons to employ Bronny and his father.

He's already proven he's worthy of a roster spot. If you're annoyed by the nepotism at play, NBA history tells us that league executives have to pay off a debt to sons of NBA players who deserved better shots.

Do you remember Mladen Sekularac?

How about Cady Lalanne, Herbert Hill, Ejike Ugboaja, Rick Rickert, Maurice Jeffers, Kris Clack and Ronnie Henderson?

These names are among the 31 No. 55 selections since the draft expanded to that many picks in 1996. Which means that one out of every four No. 55s don't even make it to Game No. 1.

That's the thing about Bronny James. Players selected this late in the draft are basically blind dart throws, unlikely to make any impact in the league whatsoever.

Any Bronny analysis has to begin with the recognition of the longshot baseline, one that shows playing in a single game is already an accomplishment. Anything after that is cake. Consider this fact: in just two seasons, Bronny has already scored the 12th-most career points of the 31 selections at No. 55.

Lakers head coach JJ Redick gave Bronny his big opportunity at the end of last season, playing him real minutes as a fringe rotation player on a playoff team. That just doesn't usually happen for players drafted as late as he was, as young as he was. In fact, among the 144 players drafted since 2000 at the No. 55 slot or later, only 15 actually played by their age-21 season, or what amounts to about 10%, according to Stathead.com research tools. Bronny is getting minutes earlier than 90% of those who are drafted as late as he was. Through this lens, Bronny is ahead of the curve.

Did Bronny benefit from being LeBron James' son and get an earlier opportunity? Sure, but such a nepotistic benefit is long overdue considering that second-generation players have been snubbed more often than not in the past. The NBA draft tells the story that NBA progeny has been underrated.

In a span beginning with the modern two-round draft's debut in 1989 and 2022, there have been 62 players selected who were the sons of an NBA player. Some became future Hall of Famers, including Stephen Curry, Kobe Bryant and Jalen Brunson. Others became perennial All-Stars and champions, including Kevin Love, Al Horford and Klay Thompson.

As I pointed out last month advocating for Carlos Boozer's son, Cam, for the No. 1 pick, sons of NBA players are nearly twice as likely to become All-Stars than their non-legacy counterparts. The reality is that sons of NBA players like Bronny James have seemingly been punished, or at the very least overlooked, by teams for having a father who played in the league.

Despite their family's starpower, Scotty Pippen Jr., Gary Payton II and Seth Curry never heard their names called on draft night and have played a combined 26 seasons in the league. Even for second-generation players who don't have a box-office last name like Luke Kornet, Garrett Temple and Wesley Matthews, the fact that their fathers played in the NBA wasn't enough to get picked.

Punished might seem like too strong of a word, but the successes of undrafted sons of NBA players lends credence to the idea that GMs stiff the name-brand prospect, preferring instead to go for lesser-known diamonds in the rough that may make them look smarter for discovering. Like GP2 and Seth Curry, it took a while for some smaller second-gen players to carve out their NBA role. Considering that Bob Myers is playing with house money getting LeBron James at just the veteran minimum this season, trading for Bronny would be a no-brainer.

It's totally possible that this was part of the deal with Philly: If I sign for the minimum, commit to trading for Bronny and I'm in. So far, there's no indication that Bronny and LeBron is a package deal, but if LeBron's happiness was truly the North Star that brought him to Philly and he wants to continue playing with his son, the Sixers' business and basketball ops shouldn't think twice about doing LeBron a solid.

LeBron James has made $584 million in his NBA career. That's a bargain. Because of the max contract that artificially caps the earning power of the best players, James has effectively subsidized the contracts of the rest of his NBA peers while providing enormous surplus value for his squad.

In a 2024 study, a BYU economist Scott Kaplan showed that James' predicted salary in 2018-19 based on ticket sales, merchandise, popularity (as represented by All-Star votes) and player performance would be a whopping $123.3 million, nearly $100 million higher than his actual salary paid by the Lakers that season ($35.6 million). And that's just value to the Lakers. Kaplan asserted that due to James' ability to fill seats on the road, his value to the entire league was worth an annualized $229 million in salary.

Instead of James getting that money, it's distributed as part of the BRI (basketball-related income) to other players. Call it the LeBron James Subsidy. Nowadays, LeBron, at 41, doesn't spin up quite as much box-office magic as he did back then when he regularly led all players in All-Star votes.

Last season marked the first time in 22 years that he wasn't voted as a starter, but he still finished with the eighth-most votes in the league. By comparison, in 2018-19, Kevin Durant ranked eighth in All-Star votes and, according to Kaplan's model, provided $182 million in value to the NBA, with $98 million allocated directly to his team.

So what will LeBron be worth in 2026-27 as a Sixer? Let's throw in the fact that the cap has skyrocketed about 60% higher than it was in 2018-19. With revenues more frothy than at the time of Kaplan's study, we can roughly project James' predicted salary for his new team to be over $150 million and nearly $300 million in total value for the NBA. And that's pegging his value to a player ranking eighth in All-Star votes like KD in 2019.

So, yeah, James' economic value to his new team will dwarf his contract, and that was before he indicated that he was willing to play for the veteran's minimum of $3.9 million. Bronny's contract will pay him $2.3 million next season which is a rounding error compared to what James' on-court and off-court value will provide. Honestly, if Bronny's younger siblings Bryce and Zhuri were both old enough and entered the draft, teams would probably consider employing them too.

Bronny remains on the Lakers roster, but the team needs to trim at least one player in order to be in line with league roster rules. By going over the roster limit, Luka's team appears to be operating as if Bronny is expendable. Perhaps they truly believe he's the next GP2, the scrappy son of an NBA player that needed a few years to find his footing, and they find a way to keep him around. But they probably know he's worth more to LeBron's new team than his old one.

Both the Lakers and Sixers have some cap work to do. According to ESPN's Bobby Marks, Philadelphia is currently $572,000 above the first apron, so they have to shed salary. Dominick Barlow's $3.4 million for Bronny's $2.3 million would get them there. It might make more sense to find a home for Dalen Terry, who is already in a logjam in the backcourt before Bronny comes into the picture.

Maybe the Lakers play hardball with the Sixers and ask for a, um, King's ransom, but then again, no team drafted him early and made the Lakers sweat in 2024 despite everyone who paid one second of attention to draft coverage knowing the Lakers would seriously consider drafting Bronny at 55.

Is Bronny getting more opportunities because of his name? Probably. But he's the exception to the rule. Usually, sons of NBA players are snubbed rather than spoonfed. LeBron is the only one who stuck around long enough to make sure the second-generation snub didn't happen to his family. After all, Philadelphia is the City of Brotherly Love. LeBron and Bronny could make Fatherly Love a reality.

title: CBS NFL analyst and former Cowboys QB Tony Romo arrested on suspicion of OWI
description: CBS NFL analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo has been arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.  According to the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office’s arrest report, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests after getting stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 on Thursday.  Sheriff’s officials said Romo was taken into custody, booked and released.
fullText:
MILWAUKEE (AP) — CBS NFL analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo has been arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while under the influence.

According to the Milwaukee County Sheriff’s Office’s arrest report, Romo performed poorly on field sobriety tests after getting stopped while driving south on Interstate 43 on Thursday. Sheriff’s officials said Romo was taken into custody, booked and released.

He has a court appearance set for Sept. 21.

Romo went to high school about 35 miles from Milwaukee in Burlington, Wisconsin.

The 46-year-old Romo has been the lead game analyst for CBS’ NFL coverage since 2017 after making four Pro Bowl appearances during an NFL career that ran from 2004-16 and was spent entirely with Dallas.

CBS had no comment regarding the arrest.

Romo remains the Cowboys’ franchise leader in career touchdown passes with 248. He held the franchise record for career passing yards (34,183) until Dak Prescott overtook him last season.
